[ASSISTANT_SAID] A chirp signal is a type of signal in digital signal processing that has a frequency that changes over time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The user aims to develop a MATLAB function called chirpTone that generates a column vector consisting of a sine wave with a growing frequency, also known as a chirp tone.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The chirpTone function takes four inputs: the duration T in seconds, the initial frequency f1 in Hz, the final frequency f2 in Hz, and the sampling rate fs in samples per second.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The output of the function is a column vector output, which contains the chirp tone with the given parameters.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To generate the chirp tone, a time vector t is created by dividing the duration T into fs equally spaced time intervals using the sampling period ts=1/fs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The frequency vector f grows linearly from f1 to f2 over the duration of the chirp tone.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The formula used to generate f is f = f1 + (f2 - f1)/(length(t)-1) * (0:length(t)-1).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This formula generates a frequency vector f of the same length as the time vector t, where the first element is f1 and the last element is f2, with intermediate values growing linearly over time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The chirp tone output is generated by taking the sine of the product of 2πf(t) and t, where f(t) is the frequency vector defined earlier.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To validate the function, it can be called with specified inputs, e.g., x = chirpTone(10,1000,2000,4000).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This example generates a chirp tone with a duration of 10 seconds, starting at 1000 Hz and ending at 2000 Hz, sampled at 4000 samples per second.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The chirp tone can be listened to using the soundsc function.
